alpha_presence_1105._why: F38#31 P2-019 (NEAR6-MS, 5 Nov 2026): judges read alpha variants as 'a modest size increase without a distinct staged presence beside the trainer'. The alpha aura's seven small pale-gold motes (11% of body radius, 0.7 peak alpha) vanish against bright Meadows grass in the judged frames. When on, the ring carries more, larger, brighter motes in the same colour, rise and orbit (alpha_aura.gd), and the alpha rim strengthens (creature_body.gd _apply_alpha_presence). Presentation only; never a size change. OFF until judged.

rest_faint_settled._why: F38#1 creature collapse and rest (CPU 5.91, qj rim075-f38-1): judges read Veridian at the resting moment as 'semi-upright' and 'splayed'. A species with no rest of its own (rest_roll_deg 0, no authored or candidate rest) rests via play_terminal("rest_faint"), which replays its faint clip from the start, so a resting creature visibly collapses and is caught mid-fall. When enabled, creature_animator.gd starts that rest at the faint clip's settled end. Presentation only; no state or collision. OFF until judged.

shiny_remake_textures._why: F39#4 (CPU 6.21; NEAR6-TW judges: shinies go near-uniform hot magenta, the lever is a colour shift on shell or plates). The remakes have no shiny texture of their own, so the shiny swap fell back to the OLD mesh's extracted shiny (different UVs) and wired it into emission too, so the whole body glowed. When enabled, creature_body._texture_for maps each live remake albedo to its own repaint (tools/art_pipeline/shiny_secondary_shift.py: only the warm secondary band moves, gold on Aquaryn's fins, jade on Cannonback's and Riptusk's plates; value, pattern, primary and glow regions kept), and each glow map to itself so only the glow lines glow. Never red. Presentation only.
shiny_remake_textures._why_on: Visual lane qj shinyplates2-f39-4 (4 Nov, CPU, three code-blind judges, calibrate.py): F39#4 shiny creature finish CPU 5.61 -> 6.76 (+1.15; raw 5.4/5.6/5.6 -> 6.3/6.3/6.4; defect PRESENT -> PARTIAL). All three judges: the violet-magenta whole-body tint is gone and shell and plate pattern survive. Judges' next lever: shiny as an accent over each species' own albedo, and keep Aquaryn's pale cyan apart from the water. Owner 4 Nov: every judged gain ships ON; a GPU High pass still closes the row.

_comment: tunable -- shiny odds (OF27). OF28 adds per-species base/shiny palettes here or in data/creatures/palettes.json; this file starts with only the roll odds because OF27 is plumbing, not colours.
_comment_phase2_shiny_finish: P2-030 production authored shiny repaints, default on under the owner's Phase 1 instruction for all thirteen staged species. No shiny odds, save, network or gameplay change. Phase 2 native ordinary/shiny comparisons and visual acceptance remain required.
_comment_emission_scale: CREATURE-PRESENTATION 2026-08-23. TUNABLE. The creature glbs ship self-lit -- the painted albedo is also the emission map, at full energy -- so in daylight every creature renders as its own texture plus an unshaded copy of itself. Measured on mudsnout: albedo hue 24 / sat 0.63 / value 0.37, rendered body a pale peach with the value contrast around the eyes gone. Halving it keeps the emission that makes a creature readable at dusk and in the Warrens while giving the colourways back their saturation and their faces. Consumed by creature_visual.gd::emission_scale(), applied in creature_body.gd::_swapped_material().
_comment_contact_shadow: CREATURE-LEGIBILITY-0903 (Gate 2.4, docs/ROADMAP.md). The 'ground-contact shadow' lever: the Compatibility renderer this project ships has no SSAO (tools/survey.sh), so nothing pins a creature's feet to the ground the way a real shadow would, and a small body in tall grass reads as standing IN the field rather than on it. A flat, unshaded, soft-edged ellipse under `creature_body.gd`'s own model origin (shaders/creature_contact_shadow.gdshader), applied to every creature body with a loaded model -- this is a grounding cue every creature is missing, not a per-species legibility tune, so unlike `field_rim`/`field_emission`/`field_degreen` it has no per-species opt-in. `radius_scale` multiplies the creature's own gameplay `radius` (never its art scale, same discipline `apply_size_multiplier`'s own header argues for -- the shadow is a fact about the collider's footprint, not a look). `opacity` is the blob's peak alpha at its centre before `core_fraction`'s falloff. TUNABLE.
_comment_field_bright_ceiling: OP-0905-03 (docs/owner/OWNER_PLAYTEST_2026-09-05.md, 'Bramblebun colour is awful'). `field_emission`/`field_degreen` (data/creatures/species.json) used to feed a raw, uncapped multiply -- at Bramblebun's shipped field_emission 2.5 that is a 3.5x push on R/B, and direct inspection (tools/_probe_field_bright_values.gd) shows these materials' un-brightened tint is already a flat white (1,1,1) over a textured base, so 3.5x pushes the coat's own mean pixel value (measured 0.49/0.37/0.21) to a mean of ~1.73 on the brightest channel -- deep in ACES's clip range, reading exactly as the owner called it: flat, washed-out, texture crushed. This is the soft-knee's target ceiling (creature_body.gd::_soft_knee_bright()): identity below the neutral 1.0 baseline (so a species with field_emission 0 is untouched), smoothly bending toward this value above it, never reaching it. 1.75 keeps Bramblebun's own brightest channel (R) at a rendered mean of ~0.85 -- comfortably under 1.0, so the coat keeps real light/shadow variation instead of clipping flat -- while still lifting every species that uses this lever meaningfully above their un-pushed baseline (Bramblebun 1.72x, Mudsnout 1.71x, Terrapup 1.63x at their shipped field_emission, per that probe's own printed numbers). A ceiling below 1.0 (floated as this key's first default) was rejected: since the baseline tint here IS 1.0, not a <1 base colour, any ceiling under 1.0 would darken every brightened species below its own normal shipped look -- reintroducing the exact 'creature disappears in the grass' problem this lever exists to fix. TUNABLE -- re-measure against tools/_probe_grass_separation.gd's render-based sweep (this pass only verified it numerically, not against a real render) before treating 1.75 as settled.

shiny_cue._why: P2-030 (F39#4, GPU 5.90, 28 Oct: the shinies 'stand small and pale against bright sand and water with no rim light or shiny sparkle cue'). When on, a shiny body (never an Aspect variant) gets a rim over its finished surfaces and the alpha mote ring (alpha_aura.gd) in pale silver-blue (creature_body.gd _apply_shiny_cue). OFF until judged.
shiny_cue.scope: local presentation only; no catch, spawn, save or network change

overlay._why: NEAR6-TW (4 Nov 2026), F39#4 (GPU 5.90): VIS-TIDEWAKE found the rim and motes do not read at the ~8 m stand (r1b/r1b2 identical, never judged). When on (with shiny_cue.enabled), a shiny's meshes also wear the character rim overlay in pale gold with a soft fill, a visible sparkle edge at stand distance. Ordinary bodies and Aspect variants are untouched. No red.
